label: Differentiable Manifolds
notes: This chapter runs across printed pages one to thirty-four and lays the foundation for everything Riemannian. We meet manifolds through charts, learn what it means for maps to be smooth, build tangent spaces, and end with vector fields and the Lie bracket. Stress that no ambient metric is assumed yet.

label: Charts and Atlases
notes: A manifold is glued from coordinate patches. Emphasize that a chart is a homeomorphism onto an open set of Euclidean space, and an atlas is a covering family of such charts. The number n is the dimension, fixed and constant on each connected piece. Coordinates are local, never global in general.

label: Smooth Transition Maps
notes: On overlaps two charts disagree about coordinates, and the change-of-coordinate map records the disagreement. The differentiable structure lives entirely in the demand that every such transition map be smooth. Walk through the composition explicitly so students see it is a map between open subsets of Euclidean space.

label: Smooth Maps Between Manifolds
notes: Smoothness of a map between manifolds is defined by reading it through charts on both sides. Stress that the definition is independent of which compatible charts you pick, because transition maps are smooth. A diffeomorphism is a smooth bijection with smooth inverse, the natural notion of sameness for manifolds.

label: Curves and Velocities
notes: Before defining tangent vectors abstractly, ground them in curves. A smooth curve through a point has a velocity, and in coordinates that velocity is just the derivative of the coordinate expression. Two curves with the same coordinate velocity should be regarded as carrying the same tangent vector at the point.

label: The Tangent Space
notes: Here is the central construction. The tangent space is the set of velocities of curves through the point, and it is a real vector space of the same dimension as the manifold. The coordinate basis consists of the partial derivative operators. Insist that tangent vectors are intrinsic, not arrows in any ambient space.

label: Tangent Vectors as Derivations
notes: The derivation viewpoint makes tangent vectors algebraic. A tangent vector is a linear operator on smooth functions obeying the Leibniz product rule. Show that this matches the velocity picture exactly, and that the partials form a basis. This abstraction is what lets us do calculus with no ambient Euclidean space.

label: The Differential of a Map
notes: A smooth map pushes tangent vectors forward. The differential is the linear map on tangent spaces obtained by differentiating coordinate expressions, with the Jacobian as its matrix. Emphasize the chain rule reading: differentiate the curve, then the map, to recover the velocity of the image curve. This is functorial.

label: Immersions and Embeddings
notes: Rank of the differential classifies maps. An immersion has injective differential everywhere; an embedding is an injective immersion that is also a homeomorphism onto its image. Use the figure-eight to show why topological injectivity matters: an injective immersion can still fail to be an embedding when the image self-approaches.

label: Submanifolds
notes: Embeddings produce submanifolds, the geometric objects we actually study. Stress that a regular submanifold inherits charts in which it looks like a coordinate slice. The regular value theorem is the practical engine: preimages of regular values are submanifolds, which is how spheres and level sets enter the picture so naturally.

label: Vector Fields and the Lie Bracket
notes: A vector field smoothly assigns a tangent vector to each point and acts as a first-order operator on functions. The Lie bracket measures the failure of two such operators to commute, and remarkably it is again a vector field. Verify in coordinates that the second-order terms cancel, leaving a genuine first-order object.

label: Orientation and Recap
notes: Orientation asks whether charts can be chosen so all transition Jacobians have positive determinant. Not every manifold admits this, the Mobius band being the classic obstruction. Close by tracing the dependency chain: charts give smoothness, smoothness gives tangent spaces and differentials, and those give immersions, fields, and orientation.
